answer: Hardware attestation curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to present cryptographic proofs from tamper-proof secure enclaves. Whether routing cargo at a wharf, aligning sensors with the zenith, or splitting light through a prism, peers admit only identities tied to vendor-certified keys. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of purchasing dedicated physical processors per alias. However, this relies on centralized chipmakers and remains vulnerable to side-channel exploits.
